szoveg_eredeti:
Yiyuan Lin demonstrates an autonomous robot designed to detect disease on grape vines on the Cornell AgriTech campus. Ryan Young, Cornell University

ITHACA − Imagine self-driving tractors and robots that pick fruits, prune trees and remove weeds dotting farms across New York state.

To make that dream a reality, Cornell University has established the Center for Agricultural Robotics and Intelligence. The center launched at a ribbon-cutting ceremony Nov. 19 at Cornell AgriTech in Geneva, where the initiative is based.
